title: Synthesize health signals and build failover chaos harness for multi-region SLO validation
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Background: We’ve seen intermittent regional failovers where autoscaling reacts slowly to correlated health regressions (e.g., KV-cache pressure + kernel stalls) and downstream clients observe SLO breaches. Existing readiness/liveness signals are noisy and not representative of tenant request shapes. Goal: create a synthetic health-signal synthesizer and a failover chaos harness to validate autoscaler stability and circuit-breaker behavior under realistic, correlated failure modes. Deliverables: 1) Health Signal Synthesizer service capable of emitting configurable multi-dimensional signals (latency histogram, error mix, token-bank pressure, connection saturation) per region and per route; 2) Failover Chaos Harness that injects staged, correlated degradations across regions (network partitions, CPU/GPU stalls, bursty token load) and measures autoscaler response, circuit-breaker trips, and SLO impact; 3) Evaluation dashboard and an automated runbook that classifies failures (transient vs sustained) and recommends configuration changes (readiness grace windows, derating thresholds, admission-backoff). Acceptance criteria: - Harness can emulate at least 5 failure patterns observed in prod incidents with >90% fidelity to key metrics; - Measured autoscaler oscillation metric reduced in post-tuning runs compared to baseline; - Playbook suggests actionable tuning changes and is reviewed by on-call and SRE; - New synthesized signals integrated into CI test matrix so every runtime change runs 3 chaos scenarios. Approach: use a lightweight Go service deployed as a Canaries namespace with a configurator UI and YAML scenarios. The synthesizer will map high-level faults to lower-level signals (e.g., "kv-pressure" -> increased kv miss ratio, elevated latencies, and sporadic 5xx). The chaos harness orchestrates traffic shaping (tc/netem), process-level pinning to create CPU stalls, and graceful shedding of synthetic tenants to observe token-aware admission. We'll collect per-request traces, autoscaler metrics (scale events, cooldowns), and circuit-breaker state transitions. Trade-offs: full fidelity is expensive; we will prioritize request-shape and kv-cache pressure as high-value axes. Risks: accidental blast radius—mitigation: isolated canary clusters, strict quota limits, and an emergency stop switch. Open questions: should the synthesizer live in test infra only or be allowed in staging with gated RBAC? Timeline: prototype (week 1–2), runbook and dashboard (week 3), integrate CI scenarios (week 4).
